clue.text: Babies played ?

parts.note: babies born three at one birth share a name with groups of three notes fitted into the time of two, which musicians play

explanation.surface: A bare question about what some infants got up to.
explanation.walkthrough: The word for babies born three at once is also a musical term: three notes squeezed into the time of two, which are played.
explanation.definitionFit: Three children born together are a set of these, and in music the same word names a group of three notes.

clue.text: Strongly suggestive of river rising by ten-fifty, possibly

indicators.note: in a down clue a rising word reads upwards, so the river's name is written backwards

parts.note: the Oder is a river of central Europe
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters may be rearranged into another order

explanation.surface: A remark that something by a river hints at a time, ten to eleven perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns ODER into REDO; 'possibly' shuffles TEN with L into LENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something redolent of a thing strongly evokes or recalls it, as a smell can call up a memory.

clue.text: Game might cause ill-feeling in the main?

definitions.text: Game might cause ill-feeling in the main?

parts.words: Game might cause ill-feeling in the main?
parts.note: the main is the open sea, where a ship rolling and heaving makes passengers seasick; the same words name a coin-throwing game

explanation.surface: A suggestion that some game could stir up resentment on the whole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' is an old word for the open sea, and 'ill-feeling' is seasickness, caused by a ship pitching and tossing; the phrase is also an old gambling game of throwing coins at a mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A gambling game in which players throw coins at a mark, the nearest then tossing all of them and keeping those landing heads up.

clue.text: Refinement, for example, in an eastern weapon

indicators.note: in tells us the abbreviation for example sits inside the weapon

parts.note: a lance is a knight's long spear

explanation.surface: Someone praising the refined look of an oriental weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegance is grace and polish of style, the quality of being refined.

clue.text: Dark-complexioned, and bashful about an excrescence

indicators.note: about tells us the bashful word goes round the growth on the skin

parts.note: shy means bashful
a wart is a small growth on the skin

explanation.surface: A dark-skinned person who is self-conscious over a lump on the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A swarthy person has a dark complexion, a synonym.

clue.text: Horse becomes quiet subsequently

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quiet
later means subsequently

explanation.surface: A horse that settles down after a while.
explanation.walkthrough: A plater is a racing term for a modest horse that runs in low-class 'selling plate' races.
explanation.definitionFit: A plater is a low-grade racehorse that competes for small plates rather than big prizes.

clue.text: Awkward situation to get into in play ?

explanation.surface: A tricky spot one might find oneself in during a game.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is the golf target: the ball is played into it on each green.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a hole is being in a fix; in golf it is the cup the ball must be played into.

clue.text: Unnecessary, fit of nervousness on vessel

parts.note: the needle is British slang for a fit of nerves or irritation
SS stands for steamship, a vessel

explanation.surface: A passenger whose anxiety aboard ship is pointless.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts the second piece below the first. 'The needle' is British slang for nerves or tension, as in a needle match.
explanation.definitionFit: Needless means not needed, the same as unnecessary.

clue.text: Olwen led fresh expression, of approval

indicators.note: fresh suggests the letters are made anew, rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A Welsh girl leads a new expression of approval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fresh' rearranges the letters of OLWEN LED.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'well done' is how one praises or congratulates someone.

clue.text: Arrange some expedition ?

indicators.note: some signals that only part of the next word is used, its letters lying inside it

explanation.surface: A request to organise part of a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' points to the letters inside expEDITion.
explanation.definitionFit: To edit is to arrange and prepare material, as for publication.

clue.text: Habitual butt, as it were?

parts.note: a butt here is the stub left after smoking, and habitual refers to the smoking habit, not to someone constantly mocked

explanation.surface: Someone who is always the target of jokes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butt' looks like a person who is always mocked, but it is the stub left by a smoker, the product of a habit.
explanation.definitionFit: The stub left after a smoke is the butt of a habit-forming product.

clue.text: It doesn't stop journalists filling extra in

indicators.note: filling means the journalists are put inside the word extra

parts.note: taken as written
the press means journalists as a body
taken as written

explanation.surface: Reporters packing additional material into a story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'filling' puts the journalists after the first two letters of the extra. The definition describes a train that runs through stations without stopping.
explanation.definitionFit: A fast train that runs past minor stations without stopping is described by this definition.

clue.text: Stay in a formation of IRA men

indicators.note: a formation is an arrangement, so the letters are arranged in a new order

explanation.surface: Republican paramilitaries staying in formation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'formation of' rearranges the letters of IRA MEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To remain is to stay or be left behind, a synonym.

clue.text: Dance band pieces

parts.note: a horn is one of a band's instruments
a pipe is another wind instrument in a band

explanation.surface: A band's repertoire of dance pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band pieces' supplies two instruments, side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A lively solo dance traditionally associated with sailors.

clue.text: Relieved by the bosses ?

parts.note: relief here is raised decoration, and bosses are knobs projecting from a surface

explanation.surface: Workers sent home by management.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relieved' looks like freed from duty, but it means decorated in relief; 'bosses' are raised knobs, not managers.
explanation.definitionFit: A surface set with raised knobs or bosses is set with studs.

clue.text: Mild concession about a form of flattery

parts.note: soft means mild or gentle

indicators.note: about tells us the concession goes round the letter a

parts.note: a sop is a small concession made to pacify someone

explanation.surface: A gentle concession that amounts to flattery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts A inside SOP to make SOAP.
explanation.definitionFit: Smooth, persuasive flattery is called this, after the gentle liquid cleanser.

clue.text: Proves attractive, but dismays East at heart

indicators.note: at heart says the letter for east goes into the middle of the word for dismays

parts.note: appals means dismays or horrifies

explanation.surface: Something that charms yet dismays the East at bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at heart' sets E in the middle of APPALS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that appeals is attractive or interesting to people.

clue.text: Oddfellows, these evangelical people?

parts.note: the ... People were an English evangelical sect, and the first word of their name also means odd

explanation.surface: A guess that members of a friendly society are evangelicals.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oddfellows are a friendly society, but 'odd fellows' points to the word meaning strange, which also named an evangelical sect, the Peculiar People.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means odd, and was the name of an evangelical sect founded in Essex, the Peculiar People.

clue.text: Christian martyrs given this VIP treatment ?

definitions.text: Christian martyrs given this VIP treatment ?

parts.words: Christian martyrs given this VIP treatment ?
parts.note: early Christians in Rome were thrown to the big cats, and the word for celebrity treatment contains those animals

explanation.surface: Martyrs being honoured as celebrities.
explanation.walkthrough: Being fêted as a celebrity is named after big cats, and Roman Christians were literally given to them in the arena.
explanation.definitionFit: To be treated as a celebrity is to be fêted, a word built on the big cats Christians were thrown to.

clue.text: Fruit or grasses

explanation.surface: A choice between orchard produce and lawn plants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grasses' is British slang for informs on, and 'peaches' is an older word for the same thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft downy stone fruits; and to peach on someone is to inform on them, as a grass does.

clue.text: Sullen cur of a crazy male

indicators.note: crazy means the letters run wild into a new order

parts.note: he is the male pronoun

explanation.surface: A sulky mongrel belonging to a mad man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crazy' rearranges CUR OF A into FAROUC.
explanation.definitionFit: A French borrowing for sullen, shy or sullenly unsociable.

clue.text: Islanders find articles under an item of litter

indicators.note: under in a down clue puts the articles below, so after, the young animal

parts.note: a cub is one young animal from a litter
ans are the indefinite article an, made plural

explanation.surface: People from an island discover reading matter beneath rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'litter' looks like rubbish, but it is a brood of young animals.
explanation.definitionFit: People from the Caribbean island of Cuba.

clue.text: Twin helps in-moving furniture

explanation.surface: A twin lending a hand with shifting the sofa.
explanation.walkthrough: Castor and Pollux are the heavenly twins of Greek myth; castors are small wheels fixed to furniture legs.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the twin sons of Leda in myth; also a small swivelling wheel under a chair so it can be rolled along.

clue.text: Strike to shield bully

parts.note: to swash is an old word for striking with a clashing blow
a buckler is a small round shield

explanation.surface: Hitting someone to protect a bully.
explanation.definitionFit: Originally a swaggering ruffian who clashed sword on shield, a bully and braggart.

clue.text: It's a rum drink

indicators.note: rum means odd, so these letters come out in an odd order

parts.note: the possessive s gives no extra letter, just the letters i, t, s

explanation.surface: A remark about a spirit drink made from sugar cane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' looks like the spirit, but it is the anagram signal meaning odd.
explanation.definitionFit: A sparkling Italian white wine from Piedmont.

clue.text: A little orchestra too ?

parts.note: LSO is the abbreviation, a little form, of the London Symphony Orchestra

explanation.surface: A small band as well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little' signals a shortened form: the London Symphony Orchestra.
explanation.definitionFit: Also means in addition, as well.

clue.text: Girl, is about ten and a quarter, they feel

indicators.note: about tells us the girl's name wraps around the number

parts.note: Anna is a girl's name
taken as written
E, east, is one of the four quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: A girl's age given as ten and a quarter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is about' puts the number inside the girl's name; the compass has four quarters, north, south, east and west, and east is the one used.
explanation.definitionFit: The feelers on an insect's head, which it uses to sense things by touch.

clue.text: Bars under a window

parts.note: bars here are measures of music, sung beneath a sweetheart's window

explanation.surface: A grille fitted below a window.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bars' look like metal rods, but they are musical bars sung by a lover beneath a window.
explanation.definitionFit: A song or piece performed at night outside a beloved's window.
